theme: 3 terms on optionals in depth: an optional that unwraps itself, transforming the value inside an optional, and a pattern that matches only real values

terms.definition: An optional written with an exclamation mark, like `String!`, that Swift unwraps for you every time you use it.
terms.example: That Implicitly Unwrapped Optional crashed because setup never ran.
terms.code:
var name: String! = "Mina"
let greeting: String = name // no ! needed
print(greeting)

terms.definition: Calling `map` on an optional, so the closure changes the value inside, and `nil` simply stays `nil`.
terms.example: Use Optional Map here instead of unwrapping, then wrapping again.
terms.code:
let price: Int? = 5
print(price.map { $0 * 2 } ?? 0)
let empty: Int? = nil
print(empty.map { $0 * 2 } ?? 0)

terms.definition: A pattern like `x?` in `if case` or `for case` that matches only when there is a value, and unwraps it.
terms.example: Loop with an Optional Pattern, so the nil scores are skipped.

quizzes.question: In this code, what do you call `s?`, which matches only the values that are not nil?
quizzes.code:
let scores: [Int?] = [3, nil, 7]
for case let s? in scores { print(s) }

quizzes.question: What lets you transform the value inside an optional, and simply keeps nil when there is none?
What do you call an optional declared with an exclamation mark that unwraps itself every time you use it?

video.description:
Learn to explain optionals in depth: Implicitly Unwrapped Optional, Optional Map & Optional Pattern, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Implicitly Unwrapped Optional - An optional written with an exclamation mark, like `String!`, that Swift unwraps for you every time you use it.
Optional Map - Calling `map` on an optional, so the closure changes the value inside, and `nil` simply stays `nil`.
Optional Pattern - A pattern like `x?` in `if case` or `for case` that matches only when there is a value, and unwraps it.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift Implicitly Unwrapped Optional, Optional Map & Optional Pattern | Day 60
landscape.description:
Explain Implicitly Unwrapped Optional, Optional Map & Optional Pattern in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
암시적 언래핑 옵셔널, 옵셔널 map, 옵셔널 패턴 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Implicitly Unwrapped Optional - An optional written with an exclamation mark, like `String!`, that Swift unwraps for you every time you use it.
한국어: 암시적 언래핑 옵셔널: `String!`처럼 느낌표로 선언해서 쓸 때마다 Swift가 자동으로 언래핑하는 옵셔널

Optional Map - Calling `map` on an optional, so the closure changes the value inside, and `nil` simply stays `nil`.
한국어: 옵셔널 map: 옵셔널에 `map`을 호출해 안의 값만 바꾸고, `nil`이면 그대로 `nil`로 두는 방법

Optional Pattern - A pattern like `x?` in `if case` or `for case` that matches only when there is a value, and unwraps it.
한국어: 옵셔널 패턴: `if case`나 `for case`에서 `x?`처럼 써서 값이 있을 때만 맞고 언래핑까지 해 주는 패턴

In this video, Mina and Jake find out why a token crashed without a force unwrap, how to change an optional without unwrapping it and how to match only real values, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.
Mina와 Jake의 채팅 스타일 대화와 화면 속 Swift 코드로 배워요.

landscape.hook: Can you explain these three optional tricks in English?

dialogue.title: It crashed without a force unwrap

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, `token` crashed the app, but I never force unwrapped it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Check the type. It's an Implicitly Unwrapped Optional.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The exclamation mark after `String`? So Swift unwraps it for me?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, an Implicitly Unwrapped Optional unwraps every time. If it's `nil`, it crashes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's Optional Map. It runs the closure only when there's a value.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So `tag` stays nil if `nickname` is nil?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Optional Map keeps the result optional.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's an Optional Pattern. It matches only a real value and unwraps it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. I'll make `token` a normal optional and check it with an Optional Pattern.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why did it crash without a force unwrap?
